newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CMB days in Bel-20 numbered - analysts.
newsitem.headline: CMB days in Bel-20 numbered - analysts.

text.p: Thursday's listing of more shares in Belgian bank Dexia CC spells the beginning of the end of shipping company CMB's presence in the Bel-20 index .BFX of leading Belgian shares, analysts said.

Some questioned, however, whether replacing one of the index's few non-financial issues with another bank was healthy for the market, noting it could speed up the debate about the creation of a wider, more representative index.
There are currently two insurers and three banks among the 20 top Belgian stocks.
"It would be no surprise if CMB were to be replaced by Dexia," Generale Bank analyst Luc Van der Elst said. "I would find that regrettable, but there are some objective rules."

Each year the bourse reviews the composition of the Bel-20 in December, adjusting it to take account of the year's trading volumes and market capitalisation at the end of November. Changes are announced in time for portfolios to be adjusted when December derivatives contracts end, this year on December 19.
According to Brussels bourse statistics, traded volume in CMB in the first five months of the year was 3.3 billion Belgian francs, ranking it 25th among Brussels forward market stocks.
Non-Bel-20 issues above it included Dexia, ranked ninth, chemicals group Tessenderlo, ranked 20th, and financial holding company Almanij, ranked 22nd.
Energy utility Powerfin, ranked 23rd, is to merge with Bel-20 stock Tractebel in October.
One non-Belgian stock, South African goldmine Freegold, was ranked 24th.

Thirty five percent of Dexia CC was listed on the Brussels bourse last November, too late for it to be included in 1996's review. An additional 15 percent was sold this month in a secondary offering, further increasing the company's free float and the liquidity of its shares.

"If nothing changes and there's no fundamental re-evaluation of CMB it's clear it will be replaced," BBL-Vermeulen Raemdonck head of research Thierry Hazevoets said. "It's clear Dexia will be in. There can be no debate about that."
CMB stock has risen two percent so far this year, lagging the Bel-20 Index, which is up around 25 percent. Dexia has outperformed the index, rising around 32 percent.
The company itself has said it hopes to enter the index.
Rather than see another industrial issue leave, some analysts said the Bel-20 should be widened. "It would be more representative of the Belgian stock market," Patrick Millecam at Corluy & Co said.
Hazevoets said there was some talk about a Bel-25 "but to what extent this would replace the Bel-20 is not clear." BBL has its own Bel-30 index.

Van der Elst said it would be a blow if Brussels' leading stock index did not maintain some non-financials, but noted it would be hard to find 20 companies large enough to create a separate industrials index.
"To do that you would have to go down into the small caps," he said.
A similar debate is raging in London where the FTSE saw two banking giants muscle their way into the blue chip index earlier this month, elbowing aside two non-financial shares.
Financial issues now make up about a quarter of the FTSE.
However the increasing predominance of financials at the expense of other sectors is in line with trends elsewhere.
The weighting of financials in Britain is smaller than that of financial stocks in Germany's DAX, but greater than their weighting in France's CAC 40.
